title: Latency investigation heuristic cheatsheet & dashboard sprint journal
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight, pragmatic cheat-sheet for investigating user-perceived latency spikes in tokenized inference and a sprint journal for iterating on a compact dashboard pack. Goal is to reduce time-to-insight for oncall and product engineers by codifying heuristics, queries, and a set of minimal panels that answer the first 90% of latency questions.

Background/context (notes to self):
- We keep seeing short-lived 95/99 spikes during early-morning traffic windows that resolve in 3–10 minutes. Root causes so far: cold KV-cache, occasional host-level GC, and an ingress retry storm from a downstream router.
- Full fidelity traces are expensive; we need a small, high-signal set of panels + a chase checklist to triage quickly.
- This is intentionally opinionated: trade breadth for speed — if the compact pack doesn't show the culprit, escalate to the long-form runbook.

Quick-investigation flow (operator-first):
1) Confirm user-visible scope: which SLO slice (region, model, tenant) hit the spike?
   - Quick query: count by tenant_id and model_name for last 15m vs baseline.
2) Surface dominant latency phase: router -> runtime -> model -> kv/cache -> network
   - Use phase_percentile panels (p50/p95/p99) for: ingress-handling, routing, model-inference, kv-read, kv-warm-up
3) Correlate traces/samples: if phase shows kv-read spikes, sample traces for kv.time > 50ms.
4) Check resource signals: GPU util, host CPU steal, node GC, iowait in same window.
5) Quickly test burst hypothesis: look at request rate derivative and per-tenant concurrency.
6) If no clear signal, enable higher-sample trace capture (5% -> 20%) for the affected tenant/model for 10 minutes.

Heuristic metric definitions (compact and operator-friendly):
- request.latency.total_ms: end-to-end API latency measured at gateway (ingress to final byte).
- request.latency.phase_kv_ms: measured time spent in KV/cache read requests (includes network to cache if remote).
- request.latency.phase_runtime_ms: token-generation CPU/GPU work time in runtime (excluding kv).
- request.latency.phase_model_ms: raw model compute time (kernel only) as reported by runtime shim.
- request.kv.miss_rate: fraction of seqs where prefix/KV miss required full recompute (0-1).
- request.kv.warmup_time_ms: time spent warming/priming cache entries for a session.
- host.gc.pause_ms: host-level stop-the-world pause proxy metric (approx from agent).
- infra.network.spike_index: synthetic metric derived from packet_rx_drops and p95 latency across nic queues.
- sampling.trace_rate: fraction of requests traced (operator adjustable).

Tracing / span annotation conventions (standardize for easy filtering):
- trace_attr: model_name, tenant_id, route, kv_hit=true|false, prefix_length, runtime_variant, gpu_model
- span names: gateway.accept -> gateway.auth -> router.route -> runtime.enqueue -> runtime.kv_read -> runtime.compute -> runtime.kv_write -> gateway.respond
- Error semantics: annotate spans with error_type and quality_tags (e.g., fallback_used=true, quantized_variant=true)
- Useful filter: runtime.kv_read.duration > 30ms AND kv_hit == false -> mark as KV-driven tail

Compact dashboard pack (minimum panels to include in sprint):
- Global overview (single row): requests/s, p50/p95/p99 total latency, error rate, sampling.trace_rate
- Slice heatmap: p95 latency by tenant x model for top-50 tenants (sparklines)
- Phase breakdown waterfall: stacked p95 of phases (kv, runtime, model, network) showing dominant contributor
- KV warmth panel: kv.miss_rate, kv.warmup_time_ms, and inferred cold_cache_events (count of requests that had warmup_time_ms > 100ms)
- Host health snips: avg GPU util, host.gc.pause_ms p95, cpu_steal p95 per node group
- Request-rate derivative: 1m-avg delta and burst detector (if > 3x baseline)
- Investigator quick-links widget: auto-generated example queries (open trace, filter traces with kv_read>30ms, open last 5 host logs)

Dashboard UX & operational notes (practical bits):
- Panels should default to 15m/1h windows; onclick drill to 3h/24h for context.
- Use tenant aliasing to avoid telemetry cardinality explosion on the heatmap (group low-traffic tenants into "long tail").
- Add a small python-based explainer: clicking a row will run 3 pre-baked queries and populate investigation template in Slack thread (PoC in linked PR).
- Add guardrails: if trace_sampling increased for a tenant, automatically create a short-lived retention index to avoid trace-cost blowout.

Sprint journal (actions & owners):
- Week 1 (owner: Marco)
  - Build phase-breakdown panel + waterfall; create helper pipeline to compute phase p95 (JIRA-OPS-8742).
  - Finish trace_attr harmonization in runtime shim (PR #407).
- Week 2 (owner: Aisha)
  - Implement kv cold event detector and panel; test on prod-staging by replaying synthetic workload.
- Week 3 (owner: Leah)
  - Instrument host.gc.pause_ms more reliably; add node tagging for quicker filtering.
  - UX polish: investigator quick-links prototype and Slack integration demo.

Acceptance criteria for MVP dashboard:
- The compact pack must surface the dominant latency phase > 80% of time for spikes that last longer than 2 minutes in our replay tests.
- Oncall can triage and create a minimal incident with root-hypothesis and one mitigation in under 12 minutes from first alert.
- Trace sampling toggle works without doubling storage costs in the first 24h (budget guardrails in place).

Open questions / trade-offs (to resolve in review):
- How aggressive should auto-escalation be when a tenant triggers high sampling? Risk: noisy tenants producing many traces.
- Do we keep kv_warmup_time on the ingest path (adds 4–6ms overhead) or derive it offline from trace reconstruction?
- Should we add a synthetic "warm-probe" per tenant during low-traffic windows to keep common prefixes primed? Cost vs benefit needs modeling.

Example queries (templated for investigator):
- top tenants by delta p95: SELECT tenant_id, model_name, p95(total_ms), p95(phase_kv_ms) FROM metrics WHERE ts >= now() - 15m GROUP BY tenant_id, model_name ORDER BY p95(total_ms) DESC LIMIT 25
- sample traces where kv-driven tail: SELECT trace_id FROM traces WHERE runtime.kv_read.duration > 30 AND kv_hit = false AND ts >= now() - 30m LIMIT 50

Notes-to-self (todo list):
- Add a short-run cost estimate for increased sampling and publish to eng-ops channel.
- Run tabletop with SRE and runtime team to validate waterfall semantics.
- Add a small "investigation template" doc that oncall fills out and attaches to incidents (owner: Jonah).

Endnotes / provenance:
- Inspired by multiple ad-hoc postmortems in Q3–Q4 2025; heavy borrow from the runtime instrumentation workshop deck.
- See linked PR for the trace_attr changes and a short demo script that populates the quick-links widget.

Unresolved syncs:
- Sync with Runtime team Wed 2026-01-15 10:30am (agenda: span naming, cost-safe sampling policy).
- SRE tabletop scheduled 2026-01-22.
